h: Railways, Red Kites and Rheidol Views
p: The Rheidol valley is one of the loveliest corners of Ceredigion, and a trip to the butterfly house is a perfect excuse to explore it. The Vale of Rheidol Railway, a narrow-gauge steam line, runs from Aberystwyth up through the valley to Devil's Bridge, chugging through woodland and along steep hillsides with views that'll keep everyone glued to the window. It runs seasonally, so check the timetable before you plan around it.

At Devil's Bridge you'll find the famous waterfalls and three bridges stacked one on top of another over a deep gorge. The walks down to the falls involve plenty of steps, so they suit older children and steady walkers better than buggies.

Bwlch Nant yr Arian, a forest visitor centre in the hills east of Aberystwyth, is the place to see red kites. Daily feeding brings dozens of these spectacular birds swooping over the lake, and it's an unforgettable sight for kids and grown-ups alike. There are also woodland trails and mountain bike routes if you fancy something more active.

For the butterfly house itself, a calm, unhurried visit works best. Stand still and you'll notice far more, from tiny camouflaged species to big showy ones feeding on fruit. Younger children love spotting the chrysalises, and it's a great way to talk about life cycles in a way that sticks. Wear light layers you can peel off, as the warm, humid air inside is a big contrast to a breezy day in the hills, and allow an hour or so so nobody feels hurried.
